name: Restaurant & food
description: Ordering, paying, allergies, and the words you hear from staff.

cards.en: Welcome (said by staff when you enter)
cards.tip: Honorific form of irassharu (to come). Staff only. You never say it back; a nod is right.
nan (how many) + mei (polite counter for people) + sama (honorific). Answer with hitori, futari, sannin.

examples.ja: 二人です。禁煙席でお願いします。

cards.tip: hitori and futari are irregular people counters; from three it is number + nin (sannin, yonin). desu completes it politely.
hitori = one person. hitori de = alone, by myself.

cards.ja: メニューをお願いします
cards.tip: noun + o + onegaishimasu. o marks the thing requested; with onegaishimasu it is often dropped: menyuu onegaishimasu.
o- + susume (recommendation, from susumeru). nan is 'what' before desu; nani elsewhere.

examples.ja: これとこれをください。

cards.tip: kore (this) + o (object particle) + kudasai (please give). kudasai is a touch more direct than onegaishimasu; both are polite.
The o- prefix makes mizu politer; it shows up on many food words (ocha, osake, okane). Both omizu and mizu are fine.
Counter goes after the particle: thing + o + number. hitotsu, futatsu, mittsu count generic objects. Add kudasai to finish.

cards.en: Said before eating (thanks for the food)
cards.tip: Humble form of 'receive'. Said once before eating, often with hands together. Also when accepting a gift.

cards.en: Said after eating / when leaving (thanks for the meal)

examples.ja: ごちそうさまでした。美味しかったです。
examples.en: Thanks for the meal. It was delicious.

cards.tip: gochisou (feast) + sama (honorific) + deshita (past of desu). Past tense because the meal is over. Casual: gochisousama.
i-adjective. Polite: oishii desu. Past: oishikatta. Negative: oishikunai. umai is the casual, more masculine version.
o- + kaikei (bill, account) + onegaishimasu. Crossing your index fingers in an X is the same request as a gesture.
betsu (separate) doubled for emphasis. de here means 'in that way'. Some places will not split a bill.
tsukaemasu is the potential form of tsukau (use): 'can be used'. wa makes 'card' the topic.

cards.ja: アレルギーがあります

examples.ja: ピーナッツのアレルギーがあります。

cards.tip: X ga arimasu = there is X, I have X. arimasu is for things; imasu is for people and animals.
taberaremasen = potential (can eat) + polite negative: cannot eat. wa marks niku as a contrast topic.

examples.ja: 持ち帰りでお願いします。

cards.tip: mochi (carry, from motsu) + kaeri (return, from kaeru). de = 'as'. teikuauto also works.
ten (shop) + nai (inside). Your answer to tennai de omeshiagari desu ka, 'for here?'.
ijou = 'that is the extent of it'. Ends an order cleanly. Also means 'the above' in writing.
